name: Facet
text: Choose a thin anchored sidebar that collapses to a tab. It stays visible enough to orient users but shrinks to save space, letting the graph dominate. Trade-off: users must click to expand details, adding one extra step. This beats a floating hover legend because it’s always reachable, not hidden until a precise mouse move.

name: Pane
text: A thin anchored sidebar still risks users overlooking it if they’re focused on the graph—especially if the tab’s icon is subtle. A persistent, full-width banner at the top (like a sticky header) guarantees visibility without hiding the graph, trading vertical space for certainty. Test both: if users miss the sidebar in 3 tasks, the banner wins.

name: Pane
text: The full-width banner risks crowding the graph when users zoom or compare data—critical for interactive analysis. A hybrid works better: a slim, high-contrast bar at the top that collapses to a single icon when unused, balancing visibility and space. Test it by measuring how often users miss controls versus how much graph they lose.
